basic_info.main_problem: I have always felt my skill in making wedding cakes is not particularly special, because anyone can master these skills through practice. This thinking pattern makes me doubt my abilities and lowers my sense of achievement.
basic_info.core_demands: These thoughts have already affected my motivation and creativity in baking, hindering my Career development and Work enjoyment, so I hope to improve self-perception through counseling, acknowledging and seeing my value and uniqueness in making wedding cakes.
growth_experiences: During the period of starting a baking career (making wedding cakes), doubting one's own skill because of a colleague's feedback; afterward often comparing with others in the industry, causing Self-doubt to worsen and satisfaction with works to decline; this pattern is especially evident when Handling wedding cake orders and after Receiving client feedback. Tried attending baking workshops and seeking client approval to ease it, but with limited effect.

During Student years, won an award for a science fair project last year. At the time, having strong interest in the project, invested much time in research and production, focusing on one's own tasks rather than comparing with others, experiencing pride and a sense of competence.

core_beliefs: My ability is not particularly special
My worth needs external recognition to hold

special_situations.event: After starting wedding-cake work, receives feedback from colleagues
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others point out my shortcomings or suggest revisions, it means I am not good enough and my skill is not special
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Attends baking workshops and doubles practice to prove oneself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Anyone can do it with practice, I have nothing particularly special

special_situations.event: In the context of handling wedding cake orders and receiving client feedback
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a client requests any change or less-than-full praise, it means my work is not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Frequently seeking clients' approval and affirmation to ease unease
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Clients may not like my work

special_situations.event: Sees works and achievements of others in the industry and compares
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my performance is not as good as others', it proves I have no value and uniqueness
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding discussing Self-doubt with friends, practicing alone extra to catch up with others
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never be as good as them

special_situations.event: In academic evaluation situations (exams, grade announcements), sees classmates performing better
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If grades are not as good as others', it means I am not smart enough and incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Studying harder, asking teachers for help, but continuing to negate one's own achievements
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not smart enough, may not be suited for this path

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be seen and recognized, expecting one's unique value to be acknowledged by others
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being negated, appearing ordinary and not good enough after comparison, thus losing the sense of value
defense_goal: Reducing Anxiety and maintaining a controllable self-image through rationalization and seeking external validation
When facing compliments, downplays the positive side to avoid the ensuing pressure and possible disappointment

object_relations.self_representation: A Student who needs to prove oneself through effort
object_relations.object_representation: A group of smarter, better classmates

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When others give praise or positive feedback on one's works or performance
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to think praise is not genuine or just polite small talk, hard to internalize as self-worth (transference: viewing others as insincere judges)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a rational, steady tone downplays praise, emphasizing 'anyone who practices can do it', and turns the conversation toward objective procedures or technical details.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When receiving neutral or constructive client/colleague feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding neutral feedback as negation or rejection, experiencing the feeling of being criticized (transference: others viewed as harsh judges)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Defensive tone, brief responses, emphasizing the other 'may not like it', and quickly seeking more external affirmation to calm unease.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When seeing peers / others in the industry with better results and comparing
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Treating Self-deprecation as fact, believing one will never be as good as others (transference: others viewed as unreachable standards)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expressing 'I cannot do it' in a self-blaming tone, lowering self-expectations, avoiding mention of one's strengths or past successes.

manifestations: Believing one's skill is not particularly special, thus devaluing self-worth and sense of achievement
Declining motivation and creativity at Work, struggling to experience meaning and satisfaction from works
Living alone and not yet discussing these specific feelings with friends, emotional support not yet fully utilized
outcomes: Inefficient use of the interpersonal support system
Relationship with colleagues affected,Increased subjective sense of isolation

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: When receiving praise, emphasizing 'anyone could do it' instead of accepting it
Focuses attention on others' standards rather than her own experience

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Understanding clients' neutral or constructive feedback as negation or dislike
Viewing others' evaluations as direct negation of one's own value

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves.
manifestations: Not discussing specific Self-doubt feelings with friends, choosing to digest alone
More self-blame than seeking help when facing pressure

exception_events.target_problem: When encountering comparison and external feedback at Work or in Learning, the client usually doubts themselves and negates positive outcomes, leading to declining motivation and creativity.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In last year's science fair project, the client did not compare with others as before, but focused and eventually won an award, experiencing pride and a sense of competence.
exception_events.reason: Clue: because of strong interest and investment in the project (different approach), focusing on the process rather than comparison (different understanding), this time produced better results and self-efficacy experience.

positive_force: Willing to attend workshops, seek help and validation
Has had success experience (winning a science fair) that can serve as evidence of self-efficacy
Having some self-Reflection ability and willingness to try reality testing
Having a few friends as potential support resources
negative_force: Evident cognitive patterns of comparison and despair
Negating positive thinking, struggling to internalize praise
Over-reliance on external validation to maintain self-worth
Heightened Self-monitoring and self-blame tendencies, reduced direct contact with others
Quick Self-deprecation upon receiving feedback, leading to declining motivation and creativity

target_behavior.behavior: Negating positive feedback and engaging in Self-deprecation in wedding-cake Work situations
antecedent: Seeing others' work in the industry and comparing
target_behavior.core_reason: The core belief 'my ability is not particularly special' and dependence on external approval, accompanied by cognitive patterns of 'negating positive thinking' and 'comparison and despair'.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding perceived failure and the discomfort of being negated, trying to temporarily relieve Anxiety through external validation.
target_behavior.consequence: Declining career motivation and creativity, reduced Work performance and satisfaction; Relationship with colleagues affected.

target_behavior.behavior: Comparing and Self-denial in academic evaluation situations, showing avoidance and low motivation
target_behavior.core_reason: A cognitive style dominated by black-and-white thinking and comparison, excessively binding achievement to self-worth.
target_behavior.function: Lowering expectations through Self-denial to reduce disappointment and Anxiety; avoiding pressure from further effort.
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased Learning drive, reduced classroom attention; avoiding peer interaction, Low mood.
